headline: Brooklyn opens transitional housing facility for New Yorkers leaving psychiatric care
dek: Bridge to Home: Brooklyn will offer private rooms, onsite behavioral-health services and housing support for up to 50 people near Woodhull Hospital.
body: New York City and NYC Health + Hospitals opened a second Bridge to Home facility in Brooklyn on Tuesday, creating a temporary housing option for people with serious mental illness who are ready to leave inpatient care but do not have a stable place to go.

The Crown Heights facility, located near NYC Health + Hospitals/Woodhull, can serve up to 50 New Yorkers at full capacity. Guests will have private rooms, onsite clinical and behavioral-health services, help with housing applications, social services and round-the-clock medical support.

Guests can stay for as long as 12 months or until they are connected with permanent supportive housing. The program is designed to keep people connected to treatment during the transition from a hospital while reducing reliance on shelters and avoidable returns to emergency or inpatient care, according to the city.

The first Bridge to Home site opened in Midtown Manhattan in September 2025. City officials said about 80% of its current guests attend weekly clinical visits and 70% have completed housing applications; among guests who moved into permanent supportive housing, the average stay was about seven months.

The Brooklyn opening brings the program's capacity to nearly 100 people at a time. Its first guests were expected to arrive during the week of the opening, giving Woodhull care teams another option for patients whose recovery depends on having a safe place to live after discharge.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Brooklyn Opens Bridge to Home Transitional Housing Facility
seoDescription: A second NYC Bridge to Home facility near Woodhull Hospital will provide private rooms, behavioral-health care and housing support for up to 50 New Yorkers.
